# GLM-5.2 model-level micro-bench

Times every operator on its own, sums them as `per-layer cost × layer count`, and reconciles that against a full-forward measurement: `ratio = roll-up / full forward`, close to 1 means the per-layer timings account for the step — not that the split inside a layer is right (see Validation). `profile_decode.py` times one step, `profile_prefill.py` times every chunk of one request's TTFT.

## Usage

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/aiter:/sgl-workspace/sglang/python
cd sikl/benchmarks/models/glm52     # required, the scripts do `import common`
```

Weights are loaded for real, so `--model` should point at a local checkout; left at its default it is a hub id and costs a 408 GB fetch.

**Prefill** — every chunk the scheduler walks to reach the first token:

```bash
python3 profile_prefill.py --model /PATH/TO/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tp-size 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.6            --ISL 100000 --reps 20
python3 profile_prefill.py --model /PATH/TO/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tp-size 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.6            --ISL 100000 --reps 20 --prefix-cache-hit 0.97
python3 profile_prefill.py --model /PATH/TO/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --dp-size 8    --ISL 100000 --reps 20
python3 profile_prefill.py --model /PATH/TO/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --dp-size 8    --ISL …[truncated]
```

# SGLang internal decode bench & profiling

Benchmark and profile **decode** of a GLM-5.2-class model by calling SGLang's internals directly —
**no HTTP server, no Scheduler, no PD path**. The harness drives `TpModelWorker` + `EAGLEWorkerV2`
itself and spawns its own TP ranks, so a data point costs ~6 minutes instead of a full server bring-up.

This directory is the **single shared copy**. It used to be three divergent copies scattered across
per-experiment workspaces; those are now under `../temp_workspace/` and hold **no code**.

```
bench/      the engine — this is what actually runs
scripts/    runners and helpers (container, single point, sweep, profile, verify)
tests/      unit tests for the engine's pure logic
```

---

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ real model weights, real MoE routing, real attention backends | |
| ✅ real EAGLE speculative decode (steps=5 / draft=6 / topk=1) | |
| ✅ CUDA-graph capture and replay, exactly as the server does | |
| ⚠️ **synthetic …[truncated]

## assistant · 2026-09-24T08:17:11.064Z

三者都绕过 HTTP server 直接调 SGLang 内部，但**测的阶段、粒度、KV 的真实性**三个维度都不同。

## 一句话区分

| | 阶段 | 粒度 | KV/输入来源 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quick_test_prefill` | 只 prefill | 整次 forward（端到端延迟 + torch profiler trace） | 真实 forward 生成的 prefix KV |
| `sglang_decode_internal_bench_and_profiling` | 只 decode | 整步 forward（稳态吞吐 + 按 stage/kernel 归因） | **合成** KV（物理合法的随机数） |
| `SIKL .../models/glm52` | prefill + decode 都有 | **逐算子**（单算子 CUDA graph 重放计时，按层数外推） | 真实权重，但输入由 forward hook 录制后单独重放 |

## 各自的定位

**1. `quick_test_prefill`** — 复用镜像内 SGLang 的 `bench_one_batch` 的 `one_batch` 路径，只加载 target 模型做一次 `extend`。核心特色是 `CACHE_HIT_RATE`：先在计时器外真实算出 `[0, cached)` 的 KV 和 DSA indexer 状态，再只对剩余 token 计时，所以 prefix cache 命中率这个口径是**真算出来的**，不是模拟的。产出 prefill 延迟、input throughput、Perfetto trace、算子/kernel CSV。没有 MTP、没有 decode。

**2. `sglang_decode_internal_bench_and_profiling`**（当前 repo）— 自己驱动 `TpModelWorker` + `EAGLEWorkerV2` 并自己拉 TP ranks，没有 Scheduler / 没有 PD。唯一带**真实 EAGLE 投机解码**（steps=5/draft=6/topk=1）和 CUDA graph capture-replay 的一个。代价是两处造假：prefix KV 是随机填的，accept length 是**驱动到目标值**而非从 draft 采样。测的是「固定 batch + 固定 context 下的稳态 decode 成本」，不是端到端 serving。一个点约 6 分钟。

**3. SIKL `models/glm52`** — 唯一做**算子级归因**的。用 `register_forward_pre_hook` 录下每个 module 的真实入参，再把单算子录进 CUDA graph 重放计时；只测 3 种代表层再乘层数外推；每个 parent 带 `<rest>` 残差行保证不丢工作量；最后用 `ratio = roll-up / full forward` 自检。还专门做了 weight rotation 避免权重被 LLC 缓存导致的虚高。decode 这边 `spec_algorithm=NONE`、显式排除 nextn 层，**不测 MTP**。它回答的是「这一步的时间花在哪个算子上」，不是「这个配置能跑多快」。

## 选哪个

- 想知道某个并发/上下文下 decode 的 TPOT、或者 EP/TP/MTP 配置对比 → 第 2 个
- 想知道 prefill TTFT、chunk 行为、prefix cache 命中收益 → 第 1 个
- 想知道时间被哪个算子吃掉了（indexer vs experts vs GEMM）→ 第 3 个

注意第 2、3 个的数都不能直接当 serving 数用：第 2 个的 accept length 是给定的，第 3 个的 decode 没有投机解码。SIKL README 里给了它对 `bench_serving` median ITL 的偏差（+5.2% @100k，+6.6% @1M），这是目前三者里唯一有外部对齐验证的。

# Spur Interactive Debug (hold a node, `spur exec` repeatedly)

For cluster basics (accounts, partition, GPU flags, Docker, gotchas) see the **spur-cluster-usage** skill. This skill is specifically about the **iterate-on-a-live-node** workflow and when to prefer it.

## The default rule

**When a task involves running or debugging something on a GPU node over more than one step, hold one allocation and `spur exec` into it each round — do NOT re-submit a fresh `sbatch`/`srun` per round.** Only fall back to per-round batch submission if the user explicitly asks for it, or the work is genuinely one-shot (single command, no iteration).

Why this is the default:
- **No re-queue, no cold start.** Each new `srun`/`sbatch` waits in the queue and starts a fresh environment. Holding a node pays that cost once.
- **Warm state survives across rounds.** A model you loaded, a compiled kernel, a warm cache, a server you started — all still there on your next `spur exec`. This is the whole point when debugging inference/training code.
- **Tighter loop.** Edit on the login node (shared NFS `$HOME` is mounted on every node), then immediately re-run inside the held node. No submission boilerplate between iterations.

## Step 1 — hold a node

Pick the GPU count the task actually needs (e.g. 8 for a TP8 model). Use a sleeper job so the allocation is independent of your terminal. **Set `-q amd-burst-qos` and don't pass `-A`** (it defaults to your account) — this is the verified-good invocation and schedules 8-GPU holds reliably:

```bash
cat > ~/hold_node.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
echo "held: $(hostname) job=$SLURM_JOB_ID gpus=$ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES"
sleep 28800   # 8h; raise/lower to taste
EOF
JOB=$(sbatch --parsable -p amd-spur -q amd-burst-qos -N1 -G8 -t 08:00:00 ~/hold_node.sh)
echo "held job = $JOB"
squeue -j "$JOB" -h -o "%i %T %N"     # wait for RUNNING, note the node
```

**If it gets held at `JobHoldMaxRequeue`, it's almost always a bad NODE_FAIL node, not your request.** A job can show `RUNNING` for one poll then requeue — that is NOT a real hold. **Always confirm with `spur exec "$JOB" true` (must exit 0).** If it keeps bouncing: capture the node each failed attempt landed on (`squeue -j <j> -h -o "%N"`), then resubmit with `--exclude=<node1,node2,...>`. A few rounds of excluding bad nodes lands you on a good one. See spur-cluster-usage's "When jobs get stuck at `JobHoldMaxRequeue`" for the full method.

`spur alloc -p amd-spur -q amd-burst-qos -N1 -G8 -t 08:00:00` also holds a node, **but the allocation dies when that command/terminal exits** — only use it inside a tmux/screen you keep open. The sleeper-job approach survives your terminal and is what you want for agent-driven debugging.

**`spur alloc` does NOT drop you onto the compute node.** Like Slurm's `salloc`, it just reserves the node and gives you a shell **on the login node** (verified: `hostname` inside an alloc returns the login node, and `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is empty). To actually get onto the reserved node you still run `spur exec <jobid> bash` — so `spur alloc` buys you nothing over the sleeper job here except a terminal you can't close. Prefer the sleeper job.

> The old advice "8-GPU nodes are unavailable, use 1 GPU" was wrong — it was really the NODE_FAIL/QOS issue above. With `-q amd-burst-qos` + excluding bad nodes, full 8-GPU holds schedule fine.

## Step 2 — iterate with `spur exec`

Each debug round, exec a command into the held job:

```bash
spur exec "$JOB" bash -c 'cd "$HOME/myproj" && python train.py --smoke-test'
spur exec "$JOB" rocm-smi                     # check GPUs
spur exec "$JOB" bash -c 'cd "$HOME/myproj" && python train.py'   # rerun after editing
```

Edit files on the login node between rounds (NFS `$HOME` is shared), then just re-run the `spur exec`. State from a *server* you launched persists only if that server is still running inside the job — start long-lived services in the background (`nohup … &`) or inside a `tmux` you started via an interactive `spur exec bash`.

For a genuine interactive shell (must be a **real terminal** — piped/wrapped `bash` gets EOF and exits immediately):

```bash
spur exec "$JOB" bash
```

## Sharp corners (verified)

- **`spur exec` runs as `root` at `pwd=/`** inside the job — always `cd "$HOME/…"` first. Your NFS home is mounted, so your code and edits are right there.
- **The `spur exec` environment is a real isolated namespace, not a thin shim.** It has its own PID + mount namespace (`ps` shows ~nothing of the host; `/proc` only lists your own namespace). Don't be surprised that you can't see the host's dockerd or other jobs' processes from here.
- **Docker still works from inside it — via docker-out-of-docker, not nesting.** The host's `/var/run/docker.sock` is mounted into the exec namespace, so `docker` here is a *client* talking to the **host** daemon. `docker run` succeeds (verified: `docker run hello-world` → exit 0), but the container it starts is a **sibling** launched by the host daemon, *beside* your exec layer — not nested inside it. Consequences:
  - `docker ps` shows **every** container on the node (including other people's vLLM). Only `rm`/`kill` your own.
  - Containers you start are owned by the **host** daemon and do **not** die when your `spur exec` or even your held job ends. Use `--rm`, or clean up manually, or you'll leak containers holding GPU/RAM.
- **GPU env var** shows as `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` in the job script, but a `spur exec` session may show it **empty** even though the GPU is present (`rocm-smi` still sees it). If a framework can't find the GPU, set it yourself in the exec command: `export ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<idx>`.
- **Interactive `spur exec bash` needs a real TTY.** No `srun --pty` and no `salloc` on this cluster (see spur-cluster-usage).
- **Docker also works straight from an sbatch script** (runs as *you* on the host, not root-in-namespace) — see spur-cluster-usage "Running Docker containers" for that path and the GPU device flags.

## Clean up

The held node stays reserved until its walltime expires or you cancel it. **Release it when done** so you're not sitting on a GPU others need:

```bash
scancel "$JOB"
squeue -u "$USER"          # confirm it's gone
```

## When NOT to use this

- The user explicitly asked for a batch `sbatch` submission (e.g. a fire-and-forget training run they'll collect later) → follow spur-cluster-usage's batch section instead.
- Truly one-shot work: a single command with no iteration → a plain `srun … <cmd>` is simpler and frees the node immediately.
- A long unattended run that must survive many hours regardless of your session → a proper `sbatch` job is more appropriate than a held debug node.

=== README ===
# sglang DSA patches

Patches that make **PD disaggregation + DP-attention** work for GLM-5.2, and,
with the fourth, **EAGLE MTP** on top. Without them the combination crashes on
the first batch or deadlocks the whole DP group under concurrency.

They apply to the sglang tree bundled in the ROCm engine images (an editable
checkout at `/sgl-workspace/sglang`). The two engine bases do **not** carry the
same arm of the set — see [Applying](#applying):

| image | base | arm |
|---|---|---|
| `Dockerfile.sglang` (gfx950 / MI355X) | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x` | 01 + dp_sync + page_table_rows + draft_dp_vote |
| `Dockerfile.sglang.gfx942` (gfx942 / MI325X) | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi30x` | **01 only**, plus a mandatory runtime flag |

| # | patch | fixes |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | `patch_dsa_indexer_hip_dp_padded_rows.py` | the HIP/aiter paged-MQA row count and `lengths` disagree — **in both directions** → `Expected lengths.size(0) == B` |
| 02a | `dsa_dp_sync.diff` | a host sync on a branch only *some* DP ranks take → collectives desync → deadlock. This file is upstream PR sglang#33973 verbatim |
| 02b | `dsa_page_table_rows.diff` | …[truncated]

## assistant · 2026-09-24T08:31:56.835Z

Research 完成，工作区与团队已就位。

## 关键结论（都是一手核对的）

**1. 真实部署的 prefill 形状**——从 packup 的 `server-info.29001.json` 直接读出，不靠 README 转述：

TP4 / DP4 / EP1 + DP-attention，`chunked_prefill_size=8192`，`page_size=64`，`kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3`，`attention_backend=dsa`，`dsa_prefill_backend=triton`，`dsa_topk_backend=sgl-kernel`，`mem_fraction_static=0.85`，aiter allreduce fusion + fused qk-norm-rope 都开，`index_share_for_mtp_iteration=true`。**prefill leg 上 `speculative_algorithm=None`**，MTP 是 decode leg 的属性，SIKL prefill 不建模它，是对的。

**2. ISL 取 100K 站得住，但必须配一个高 prefix cache hit**——这是我从 packup 里挖出来的最重要的一点：

| | |
|---|---|
| input tokens p50 | **110,498**（mean 145,279，被 std 128K 的长尾拖高） |
| `prompt_total` | 1,213,744,966 |
| **实际 `computed`** | **38,930,768 = 3.21 %** |

真实部署里 prefill 只算了 3.2% 的 prompt token，其余走 radix/HiCache 前缀。所以只跑 `--prefix-cache-hit 0` 会量出一个生产中根本不存在的形状。我跑两个点：

- **A（对齐生产）**：`--ISL 100000 --prefix-cache-hit 0.96`
- **B（冷参照）**：`--ISL 100000 --prefix-cache-hit 0`

B 不是多余的——没有它，A 的排名无法解释。

**3. 镜像不在 256 上。** 部署用的 `infera-sglang:v0519-yihou-0917-nextnfix-hicache` 节点 256 没有，但它的 base `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260916` 有（我跑起来验过，报 `0.5.19.dev20260916+ge7f7447333`）。**不搬也不重建那 91 GB**，改成：跑 base + 运行时只打 `sglang_dsa` 那一组补丁。理由是 patch 01 修的正是 DSA indexer 在 **DP attention** 下的 paged-MQA 行数，`dsa_dp_sync` 防 DP 组死锁——这两个在我们这个形状上是承重的；而 Mooncake / disagg / Responses / HiCache / NextN 那几层，SIKL 这种无 server、无 PD、单腿的 micro-bench 根本走不到。验收门槛是脚本自带的 7 个 **bytecode** marker，不看源码文本。

这是一个**声明的偏差，不是等价性主张**（再加 0916 vs 0917 nightly 的版本差），会写进报告。

## 已就位

- 工作区 `infera.glm52.pd/yihou/glm52.sikl-prefill-hotspot.yihou_20260924/`，所有实验活动都在里面
- `spec/mission.md` 任务书；10 分钟注入一次（cron）
- `CLAUDE.md` 新建于 `infera.glm52.pd`（该仓库原本没有，无需备份；当前 worktree 的 `.claude/CLAUDE.md` 是另一个仓库的 DCO 规范，我没动）
- 团队：`env-runner` 正在起容器、打补丁、跑 ISL=8192 的小 smoke；`watchdog` 每 3 分钟巡检。leader 每 20 分钟轮询，首次发现问题只记录，下次仍未解决才介入

一个提醒：node 256 上还跑着别人的容器 `codex_moe0922_ut_256_merge0924`，已写进规则不碰。

权重加载 + 冷 triton JIT 首次可能要 20–40 分钟且**看起来像挂了**，我会按进度判断而不是按时间判断。有结果我再报。

    """Resolve the FP8 scale layout DeepEP v2 must pre-quantize into."""
    from sglang.srt.layers import deep_gemm_wrapper

def latency_test(
    server_args,
    port_args,
    bench_args,
    gpu_id,
    tp_rank,
):
    cfg = resolving_view(server_args)
    # `main` runs this inline for tp_size == 1 and spawns it per rank otherwise;
    # a spawned child arrives with nothing published.
    publish(server_args, role="scheduler")
    initialize_moe_config()
    initialize_fp8_gemm_config()
    initialize_fp4_gemm_config()

    if get_bool_env_var("SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY"):
        parallel = get_parallel()
        set_gpu_proc_affinity(
            parallel.pp_size,
            parallel.tp_size,
            parallel.nnodes,
            tp_rank,
        )

    # Configure the logger
    configure_logger(server_args, prefix=f" TP{tp_rank}")
    rank_print = print if tp_rank == 0 else lambda *args, **kwargs: None

    # Load the model
    model_runner, tokenizer = load_model(server_args, port_args, gpu_id, tp_rank)

    # Prepare inputs for warm up
    reqs = prepare_synthetic_inputs_for_latency_test(
        bench_args.batch_size[0], bench_args.input_len[0]
    )

def setup(server_args, port_args, gpu_id: int, tp_rank: int, tag: str = "BENCH"):
    """Build the model. Returns (model_runner, rank_print).

    rank_print prints only on rank 0 and tags every line, so the output stays
    findable in the JIT compiler's chatter.
    """
    from sglang.benchmark.one_batch import load_model
    from sglang.srt.layers.moe import initialize_moe_config
    from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp4_utils import initialize_fp4_gemm_config
    from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils import initialize_fp8_gemm_config
    from sglang.srt.utils import configure_logger

    initialize_moe_config(server_args)
    initialize_fp8_gemm_config(server_args)
    initialize_fp4_gemm_config(server_args)
    configure_logger(server_args, prefix=f" TP{tp_rank}")

    bench_runner, _ = load_model(server_args, port_args, gpu_id, tp_rank)

    if tp_rank != 0:
        return bench_runner.torch_runner, lambda *a, **k: None

    def rank_print(msg=""):
        print("\n".join(f"[{tag}] {ln}" for ln in str(msg).split("\n")), flush=True)

    return bench_runner.torch_runner, rank_print

崩溃点是 `initialize_moe_config() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given`。但**真正的坑不是签名**：

这版 sglang（`0.5.19.dev20260916+ge7f7447333`）把运行时配置搬到了一个 **published context** 后面——`runtime_context.py::publish(server_args, role=...)`。之后 `initialize_moe_config()` 改为从 `get_exec()/get_spec()/get_flags()` 读，不再收参数；两个 GEMM 初始化函数同样。

所以**如果只是把参数删掉，比崩溃更糟**：镜像自带的 `sglang/benchmark/one_batch.py::latency_test`（903–909 行）在同一位置写着注释 *"a spawned child arrives with nothing published"*——spawn 出来的 TP 子进程什么都没 publish，不调 `publish()` 的话 MoE/量化 flag 会**静默回落到默认值**，而不是我们的 server_args。那恰好会污染 `mlp.experts` 这一行——这个 bench 存在的意义就是量它。这点我是在写修复之前查的，不是之后。

## 处理

- SIKL 仓库不动（mission 规则 5）。把 bench fork 到 workspace 的 `scripts/sikl-glm52-yihou/`（SIKL HEAD `82dd439d`），只改 `setup()` 的开头，对齐 `latency_test` 的 prologue，patch 里按行号注明了权威出处。diff 存 `patches/sikl_common_publish.yihou.diff`。
- 让 `env-runner` **先做一遍全量 API 代差扫描**（用 `inspect.signature` 把 fork 里所有 sglang/aiter 符号跟镜像对一遍）再重跑。逐个撞、撞一次赔一次 bring-up，不划算。

## 另一件事，比崩溃更值得记

wrapper 在 4 个 TP 子进程全死的情况下报了 `SMOKE_EXIT=0`。子进程死亡不会透传到这个脚本的退出码，**退出码在这里不能当通过信号**。已改成：产物存在 **且** 日志里没有 `Traceback` 才算过。这个假绿要是没被 watchdog 顺手抓到，后面很可能拿着一份空报告往下走。

## 顺带确认的好消息

- DSA 补丁门槛 **7/7 bytecode marker 全过**（不是看源码文本）
- 15 个 server_args flag 全被接受，`--dsa-prefill-backend triton`、`--dsa-topk-backend sgl-kernel` 都在——round 000 留的那个 open item 关掉了
- 无 `Memory access fault` / `NCCL` / `Segfault` / OOM，8 卡状态正常

## assistant · 2026-09-24T08:42:18.832Z

env-runner 报回来一条**会改结果的更正**，我核实后确认它对、**我的 mission 写错了**。

## 更正：chunk size 应该传 32768，不是 8192

我之前从 `server-info.29001.json` 读到 `chunked_prefill_size: 8192` 就当成了 CLI 值。那是**除完之后的 per-rank 值**。三路独立验证：

1. 镜像里 `srt/arg_groups/parallel_hook.py:198`——开 DP attention 时解析阶段做 `chunked_prefill_size // dp_size`
2. packup 自己的 `config.sh:49` 是 `PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE=32768`，经 `engine.sh:168` 原样传下去；32768/4 = 8192 ✓
3. env-runner 留了个未决问题：SIKL 会不会再除一次？我查了——`common.py::chunk_tokens()` 读的是**已解析**的值，**不会二次相除**，`chunk_flag()` 只是为了报告标签再乘回去

要是没抓到，每个 chunk 都会在**部署的四分之一尺寸**下跑，而且跑得出来、看着也合理——但哪个算子显得热会跟着变。这是它这轮最有价值的产出。mission 已改。

## 另一个被我提前挡掉的坑

env-runner 问："SIKL 在 `load_model` 之前调这三个函数，我没验证子进程那时有没有 publish 过 ServerArgs——只删参数可能只是把失败挪后。"

答案是：**子进程确实没 publish**，而且后果比它设想的更糟——只删参数不会失败，会**成功且错**：MoE 和量化 flag 静默回落到默认值，而不是我们的 server_args，污染的正是 `mlp.experts` 那一行。镜像自带的 `one_batch.py::latency_test` 903–909 行就写着 *"a spawned child arrives with nothing published"*，并在三个初始化前调 `publish(server_args, role="scheduler")`。我的 patch 照抄它。

它独立扫出的三个不兼容符号跟我的 patch 范围完全吻合，算一个交叉验证。

## 其他已接受的偏差

- **用 GPU 4-7 而非 0-3**：另一租户的容器钉在 GPU 0，共用会互相污染。MI355X 同构、单腿计算 bench 无 RDMA，卡的身份不影响 kernel 计时；NUMA1 只影响 host 侧权重加载。记录，不为它花 GPU 时。
- **AITER JIT cache 放 `/mnt/m2m_nobackup`**：节点根分区已用 93%，只剩 9.1 GB。
- 这台机上 `spur exec` 以 `yihou` 身份跑，不是 root。

现在等 round 001b 的 smoke 和它的 `ratio`。100K 两个点还没放行。

## `[AR] ... custom AR disabled` 是 world group 在说话，不是 TP group

`parallel_state.py:507` 的那行在一个 `elif` 里：只要某个 GroupCoordinator 是用 `use_custom_allreduce=False` 建的、且 `world_size > 1`、且在 HIP 上，就无条件打印。而 2089 行显示 `group_name="world"` 是**硬编码** False 的——我们的 world group 正好是 4，所以必打，跟我们传什么 flag 无关。

模型真正用的 TP group 走 `init_model_parallel_group(use_custom_allreduce=None)`，回落到模块全局 `_ENABLE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE`（默认 True，由 `bootstrap.py:201` 从**已 publish** 的 context 里取 `disable_custom_all_reduce`——正是我那个 patch 填上的）。

Watchdog 自己的观察反而是佐证：**每 rank 只有一行，不是两行**。TP group 若也被关，应该出现第二行。

另外 `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` 是另一套机制（把 all-reduce 和相邻的 norm/residual 融掉），不是 custom-AR kernel 的替代品，那行日志对它不置一词。

一个值得记的不对称：部署的 **prefill leg 是 `disable_custom_all_reduce=False`，decode leg 才是 True**。这里以 prefill 为准，不能照抄 decode。

**没有结案**：已要求 round 2 在 rank 0 上运行时断言 `get_tp_group().ca_comm is not None`，若为 None 就停。真要是回落成裸 NCCL，误差会直接落进 SIKL 的 `layer.<rest>` 和 `mlp.<rest>` 两行。

## env-runner 推翻了我的一条指令，它是对的

我让它把 `/workspace/SIKL` 放进 `PYTHONPATH`。它发现 **SIKL 自带一份 vendored aiter（205 个路径不同）**，照我说的做会让 `import aiter` 解析到 SIKL 那份——那就变成在量 **SIKL 的 MoE kernel，而不是部署实际跑的那个**。它把 `/workspace/SIKL` 摘了。代价只是 `sikl` 包不可导入、SIKL schema dump 用不了，本任务不需要。

这是它第二个能把结果悄悄带偏的发现，会写进报告的 deviation 一节。

## 点 A 通过，`ratio = 0.996`，并且给出了这次最值钱的发现

**先说三个已经关掉的悬案：**

- **AR 断言 CLEAR**：`tp_group.ca_comm = True`。之前那行 `custom AR disabled` 确实是 world group 在说话，TP group 走的是部署同款 collective 路径。这条从"读码推断"升级成了"运行时实测"。
- **cache hit 生效**：`chunk 1/1: 3232 new on 96768`，正是你要的模拟。
- **triton 在 fp8 分支上解析**，已是一手证据。

## 热点排名（点 A，对齐部署形状）

| 算子 | ms | 占比 |
|---|---|---|
| `attn.<rest>`（qk_norm+rope+absorb_bmm+kv_write+attn kernel） | 165.97 | **30.4%** |
| `mlp.experts` | 103.76 | **19.0%** |
| `mlp.<rest>` | 72.38 | 13.2% |
| **`attn.indexer`** | **66.43** | **12.2%** |
| `layer.<rest>` | 56.63 | 10.4% |
| `attn.o_proj` | 42.02 | 7.7% |

## 发现：indexer 的开销跟着它扫的 prefix 走，不跟它算的 chunk 走

`attn.indexer` 从 smoke 的 1.7% 跳到 12.2%——绝对时间 **19.17 ms → 66.43 ms，而 chunk 反而小了 2.5 倍**（8,192 → 3,232）。

**这恰恰是 cache-hit=0 的跑法量不出来的东西。** hit=0 时 prefix 和 chunk 一起长，indexer 对 context 的依赖被混淆掉了。点 A 把它分离开——小 chunk 压在大的已驻留 prefix 上，而这就是生产形状。你坚持要模拟命中率，这是它兑现的地方。

**但我没让它结案。** 点 A 是两次不同 ISL 的跑出来的两个点，不干净。点 B 才是这个claim 的**受控实验**：13 段、chunk 固定 8,192、prefix 从 0 扫到 98,304——只动 prefix。我已要求它交出 `attn.indexer` 的逐段序列，外加一条纯 GEMM 行作对照（那些行的工作量只跟 chunk 有关，而 chunk 全程不变）。indexer 爬、对照行平 → 成立；indexer 也平 → 点 A 的跳变另有原因，那更得先知道。

## 两条挂着的限定

- `ratio=0.996` 只证明**没漏掉工作量**，不证明层内拆分对。单 chunk 是弱检验，点 B 的 13 段才有牙齿。
- `attn.kv_b_proj` 全程未触发（100,000 远超 2,048 dense 阈值，走 `mla`）。点 B 的第一段（0→8,192）是两个点里唯一可能出现 dense 的位置，会明确回答，不留空行。

## 一条我标为 OPEN、不许草率关掉的

点 A 的 3,232 token 用了 548.9 ms，折算到部署平均 ~4,663 实算 token 约 0.79 s，而实测 TTFT p50 是 **3.60 s**。中间的差距**看起来**能被排队、40 路批处理、radix 查找、HiCache host→device 加载吃掉——但这里一样都没量过。在有人真正拆开之前，不能说这两个数"对得上"或"对不上"。

点 B 在跑，13 段 × ~17 算子 × 20 reps，比 A 的 13 分钟长不少。

两个理由，第二个才是促使我下这个决定的：

**1. 点 A 前五行里有三行是 `<rest>` 行。** SIKL 自己的 README 说：同配置相隔几分钟重跑，step time 复现到 0.05%、直接测量的行 0.2–0.5%，但 `<rest>` 行能飘得多得多（`layer.<rest>` 3%，接近零的 `mlp.<rest>` 52%）。而 `attn.indexer` 12.2% 和 `mlp.<rest>` 13.2% 只差 1 个点——**没有重复跑，我没法诚实地说这两行分得开**。

**2. Watchdog 报 GPU 0-3 有 27–28% 利用率——那是另一个租户的容器。** 我们的 TP 组是 4-7，它们的计算碰不到我们，但**主机和 XGMI fabric 是共享的，而这里没有任何测量说这份争用为零**。我不打算假设它为零。隔一段时间、在不同邻居负载下重跑一次 A，是现成最便宜的证据：两次吻合，这个担忧就被测量框住了而不是被话术绕过去；两次不吻合，那本身就是必须在任何人引用排名之前落地的发现。

A2 要求按**逐行 diff** 报（每行 ms、delta%、ratio），并明确点出两次之间**排序发生变化**的行。

## 另外记了两条环境事实

- **权重加载在 rank 之间差了 2.5 倍**：TP1 186 s、TP2 189 s、**TP0 460 s**——同一个 408 GB 模型、同一次跑。不是故障，也没碰到测量，但以后排期要按最差 rank ~460 s 算，不是 ~190 s。
- aiter JIT cache 保持 218 MB 且**被复用**，冷编译只在 smoke 付过一次。

点 B 在跑。

with `X.<rest> = X − sum(children)`. So an error δ in the measured `attn` parent enters `attn.<rest>` at **+δ** and `layer.<rest>` at **−δ**. Exactly as you say.

## 2. SELF-CONTRADICTION — the README-band bullet survived the fix

Lines 165–176 now say, correctly, "**we do not meet it**" and name the three rows that exceed 0.5 %. But the bullet at lines 207–210 still says the README "puts run-to-day movement at 0.2-0.5 % for directly measured rows … **the A/A2 pair is consistent with that**."

## 3. OVERSTATEMENT — "the deployment shape is exactly where the indexer is relatively most expensive"

Not supported by the numbers:

| | indexer share |
|---|---|
| A (production hit 0.9679) | **12.16 %** |
| B, aggregate over the sweep | 7.76 % |
| B, chunk 12 (deepest full chunk) | **13.64 %** |
| B, chunk 13 (1,696 tokens) | 11.64 % |

A is **higher than B's average but lower than B's deepest chunk.** The defensible claim is that the production shape puts the indexer *well above the whole-prefill average* — 12.2 % vs 7.8 % — because production pays the deep-context part without the shallow early chunks that dilute it. Not that it is the maximum; B's deepest chunk beats it.

Suggest: "…so the production shape sits near the top of the indexer's range rather than at the average — 12.2 % against 7.8 % averaged over a cold prefill, and close to the 13.6 % of the deepest cold chunk."

## 4. UNVERIFIED ASSERTION — "NUMA1 affects host-side weight load, not kernel time"

Deviation 3 states this as fact. **I never measured NUMA topology and cannot confirm GPUs 4-7 sit on NUMA1**, nor that kernel time is unaffected. The second half is a reasonable expectation; the first half is an assumption about this node's layout.

It is also in tension with the next item. Suggest reducing it to what we have: *"MI355X is homogeneous, so GPU identity is not expected to move a kernel timing. Host-side placement may differ between GPU groups; this was not measured."*

## 5. MISSING DEVIATION — the bench does not set CPU affinity, though the image asks for it

Found while writing the reproduction steps, and confirmed first-hand.

The image sets **`SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1`**. This image's own `one_batch.py::latency_test` honours it, and the block sits **between the three initialisers and `configure_logger` — i.e. inside the exact span our publish patch reproduced**:

```python
if get_bool_env_var("SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY"):
    parallel = get_parallel()
    set_gpu_proc_affinity(parallel.pp_size, parallel.tp_size, parallel.nnodes, tp_rank)
```

Neither our fork **nor upstream SIKL** calls `set_gpu_proc_affinity` (grepped both: absent). So the bench leaves its rank processes unpinned where the engine path under the same env would pin them. Our patch is still a faithful re-sync of the *config* prologue — the omission is upstream SIKL's, not something the patch introduced — but the difference is real and belongs in the Deviations list.

## 结果：GLM-5.2 prefill 的热点，以及一个结构性结论

**生产形状（点 A：ISL 100K，cache hit 0.9679，实算 3,232 token，`ratio` 0.996）**

| 算子 | ms | 占比 |
|---|---|---|
| `attn.<rest>`（qk_norm+rope+absorb_bmm+kv_write+**注意力 kernel**） | 165.97 | **30.4%** |
| `mlp.experts`（MXFP4 fused MoE） | 103.76 | **19.0%** |
| `mlp.<rest>` | 72.38 | 13.2% |
| **`attn.indexer`** | **66.43** | **12.2%** |
| `layer.<rest>` | 56.63 | 10.4% |
| `attn.o_proj` | 42.02 | 7.7% |

**真正的发现来自受控实验（点 B：chunk 固定 8,192，prefix 扫 0→90,112）：整张表只有 `attn.indexer` 在涨，9.2 倍；连注意力 kernel 本身都是平的。**

注意力 kernel 平，正是稀疏注意力在起作用——过了 top-2048，它每个 query 只打固定预算；要长的是 indexer 那趟"从全上下文选出这 2048 个"的扫描。**所以这个模型里长上下文的代价集中在一个算子上，而且不是 attention。** indexer 只跑 21/78 层。

一条留给后续的线索：indexer 在 chunk 8（prefix 49,152→57,344）有个 **+37.83 ms 的一次性电平跃迁**，是其余十步均值的 3.25 倍，而紧随其后的一步是全场最小——像 triton DSA 路径的 tiling 边界。没查，不认领原因。

## 关于你那句提醒

你说"要模拟 cache hit rate，不然结果没任何意义"——这话在数据上得到了印证。indexer 在冷跑（hit=0）全程平均只占 7.8%，在生产形状下是 12.2%。**冷跑会把这个算子的重要性系统性地低估掉**，因为 prefix 和 chunk 一起长，把它对 context 的依赖混淆了。

## §3 — BROKEN. `patch -p0 < diff` applies nothing.

You were right to doubt it. Tested on a fresh copy of pristine SIKL:

```
$ cd <fresh copy> && patch -p0 --dry-run < patches/sikl_common_publish.yihou.diff
Ignoring potentially dangerous file name /home/yihou/.../scripts/sikl-glm52-yihou/common.py
can't find file to patch at input line 3
Skipping patch.
1 out of 1 hunk ignored
exit=1
```

Cause: **both diffs carry absolute paths in their headers**, because I generated them with `diff -u <abs> <abs>`. `-p0` strips nothing, so patch looks for `/home/.../patches/common.py.orig` (which does not exist — there is no `.orig` in `patches/`, only the two `.diff`s) and then for the absolute target. Modern GNU patch refuses the absolute path outright. **cwd is irrelevant**, so the `cd` in the instructions buys nothing.

Silver lining: the failure is safe, not destructive. It refuses rather than silently re-patching the real fork, which is what I feared when I set the test up with `--dry-run` first.

**Tested fix — name the target file explicitly, which overrides the header:**

```bash
cp -r /home/yihou/dev/git/SIKL/sikl/benchmarks/models/glm52 "$WS/scripts/sikl-glm52-yihou"
cd "$WS/scripts/sikl-glm52-yihou"
patch -p0 common.py < "$WS/patches/sikl_common_publish.yihou.diff"
patch -p0 common.py < "$WS/patches/sikl_common_allreduce_assert.yihou.diff"
```

I ran exactly this on a fresh copy and diffed the result against the fork the three runs used:

```
dcb56beec20e4adfa45ed9aa63fc4e68  <rebuilt>/common.py
dcb56beec20e4adfa45ed9aa63fc4e68  scripts/sikl-glm52-yihou/common.py
```

**Byte-for-byte identical.** So the two diffs do apply cleanly in that order and do reproduce the exact fork — the instructions were the only thing wrong. As you asked: fix the instructions, not the diffs.

One more §3 trap: `cp -r SRC DST` when `DST` already exists puts the copy *inside* as `DST/glm52`. The command only works against a non-existent path. Either say so or use `cp -r SRC/. DST/`.

## §5 — does not match how I ran them, and it matters for the verdict

Documented:
```bash

```

  bash -c 'bash /workspace/ws/scripts/round2-run.sh A > /workspace/ws/logs/round2-A.log 2>&1'
```

Two differences, both load-bearing:

1. **`-d`.** The documented form runs in the **foreground**. Point B is ~28 minutes; over a `spur exec` that dies with the exec. Every run here was detached.
2. **Where the redirect lives.** You spotted the right hazard. The script's verdict greps `$LOG` = `/workspace/ws/logs/round2-A.log`. With the redirect *outside* the container, the host shell owns the file handle and the script greps a file the host is still buffering into — the last lines, including any late traceback, may not be on disk when the grep runs. With the redirect **inside** the container, the script's own shell owns it and the grep sees a complete file. The verdict is only trustworthy in the second form.

Also: §0 says access is `spur exec <jobid>`, but §1/§2/§5 show bare `docker` commands. One line saying "every `docker` command below runs via `spur exec <jobid> ...`" would close that gap for an outsider.

# Experiment result pack-up

## Purpose

An experiment is only valuable if someone else (or future-you, six months from now, on a fresh machine) can **reproduce it cold**. This skill turns a pile of scratch — a spec markdown, a `working_process.md` log, timestamped result dirs, half-remembered debugging fixes — into one clean, self-contained deliverable folder that captures *everything* needed to re-run the experiment and trust the numbers.

The deliverable is not a summary. It is a reproduction kit. The test is simple: **hand the folder to a stranger with cluster access and they should be able to reproduce the result without asking you a single question.**

## When this triggers

The user has done real work (benchmark / perf sweep / debug session / ablation) and signals a milestone: "整理成果", "pack this up", "write this up", "make it reproducible", "archive the results", "produce a deliverable". Even a terse "整理一下" in an experiment context counts — err toward triggering.

## Two hard rules (read before touching anything)

1. **Never delete original experiment files** — not local, not remote, not the workspace, not the containers, not the logs — unless the user *explicitly* says so. You are *copying and synthesizing*, not moving. The original mess stays exactly where it is. When in doubt, copy; never `mv`, never `rm`.
2. **Ask before committing heavy or sensitive artifacts.** The deliverable may be committed to git. Before including any file **> 4 MB**, ask the user. Logs can be huge and are often the crux of a debug story — **ask the user whether they want log files included** (and if so, whether trimmed/gzipped). Never pack real secret *values*; record only *which* secrets are needed and where they come from.

## Workflow

Work through these phases in order. Use a task list to track them — a pack-up touches many sources and it's easy to drop one.

### Phase 1 — Gather the sources

Find and read every input that describes what was done. Typical sources:

- **The spec / task file** the user handed down — usually a `*.md` (e.g. `dsv4_bench_sglang_pd_align.md`). This is the *purpose*. Also check `CLAUDE.md` for the "current task" pointer.
- **The working-process log** — `*.working_process.md`. This is the *narrative*: what was tried, what broke, what fixed it, the wrong turns. Read it fully — do not skim.
- **Result directories** — timestamped dirs like `bench_results/<name>_<ts>/`, each typically holding `scripts/`, `out/`, `logs/`. These are the *evidence*.
- **Your memory** for this project (`memory/MEMORY.md` and linked files) — feedback, gotchas, decisions not written elsewhere.
- **Conversation history** — corrections and constraints the user gave live-only.

If a source is ambiguous or missing, note the gap explicitly rather than inventing content. "env driver version not captured" is more honest and more useful than a confident guess.

### Phase 2 — Build the deliverable directory

Create the deliverable **in the same folder as the experiment**, dated:

```
<experiment-name>.packup_YYYYMMDD/
├── README.md            # entry point: what/why/result at a glance + navigation
├── REPRODUCE.md         # THE reproduction kit — exact ordered steps, copy-pasteable
├── environment.md       # hardware + software env, pinned versions, SHAs
├── scripts/             # every script needed to reproduce (copied verbatim)
├── patches/             # fixes/patches applied, each with a what/why/how note
├── results/             # the numbers: CSV/PNG/summary tables (evidence)
├── notes.md             # gotchas, wrong turns, error analysis (what/why/how/context)
└── logs/                # OPTIONAL — only if user opts in (may be trimmed/gzipped)
```

See `references/deliverable_layout.md` for the full annotated structure and ready-to-fill `README.md` / `REPRODUCE.md` templates.

### Phase 3 — Fill each file (the seven things reproduction needs)

See `references/checklist.md` for the authoritative field-by-field checklist. The seven essentials:

1. **Time** — when it ran (date range + per-run timestamps). Convert relative dates to absolute.
2. **Purpose + the spec** — *what* it set out to prove and its success criteria. Copy the spec markdown in (or link by exact path if too large). README states the goal in 2-3 sentences.
3. **Environment** — the single biggest reproducibility trap. Capture both:
   - **Hardware**: exact machines/hostnames, GPU model + count, CPU, RAM, and — critically — **driver versions and the RDMA fabric** (IB / ionic / RoCE config + driver versions, active rails). Use `scripts/collect_env.sh`.
   - **Software**: docker image tag **and** base-image `sha256` digest, the Dockerfile, and the **git branch + commit SHA**. Pin everything — a floating `:nightly` tag is not reproducible.
4. **Exact reproduction commands / scripts** — copy the real scripts **verbatim** into `scripts/`; `REPRODUCE.md` lists the ordered command sequence. Include **debug/fix outcomes**: if it only worked after a fix, the fix is *part of* the reproduction — put patches in `patches/` each with **what / why / how / context**.
5. **Dependency absolute paths / uncommitted files** — model weights on shared storage (absolute path), datasets, uncommitted config, injected host libs (e.g. `libionic`).
6. **Required secrets** — enumerate *which* creds the run needs and *where they come from* — never the values.
7. **Explanatory doc (notes)** — `notes.md`: caveats, gotchas, wrong turns, error analysis as **what / why / how / context**. Often the most re-read file.

### Phase 4 — Verify the kit is self-contained

Cold-read pass: pretend you know nothing and read only the packup. Can you reproduce it? Check: `REPRODUCE.md` references only files inside the packup or clearly-marked external absolute paths; every referenced script exists; every version/SHA/path is concrete; the success criteria are restated with the actual result against them.

Then report: the deliverable path, a one-paragraph summary, and any gaps flagged (missing env capture, logs left out pending decision, files > 4 MB awaiting approval).

## Bundled resources

- `scripts/collect_env.sh` — snapshots hardware + software env on a node (GPU/driver, RDMA rails, docker image digest, git branch+SHA, CPU/RAM). Run on each machine, paste into `environment.md`.
- `references/deliverable_layout.md` — full annotated layout + README/REPRODUCE templates.
- `references/checklist.md` — authoritative completeness checklist; walk it before Phase 4.

## assistant · 2026-09-24T10:22:15.915Z

查清楚了，而且这个问题戳到了我们自己测量的一个缺口。

## prefill 的 batch size 是什么

**chunk 预算是 token 预算，不是请求预算。** 这些 token 怎么分给请求，是一个自由变量。`quick_test_prefill` 的做法（`prefill.py:100-102`）：

```python
chunk_len = args.input_len
if local_bs * chunk_len > cfg.chunked_prefill_size:
    chunk_len = cfg.chunked_prefill_size // local_bs // page * page
```

`local_bs` 个请求**共享一次 forward**，每个分到 `预算/local_bs` 个新 token，总量仍 ≤ 预算。所以同样是 8192 tokens 一次 forward，可以是：

- **1 个请求 × 8192 token**（我们测的：ISL 100K，一个长请求自己吃满预算）
- **4 个请求 × 2048 token**（多个请求同时在推进，各走一点）

## 为什么这两个形状**开销不同**

GEMM 只认总 token 数（M 维），两种形状一样。**但 indexer 不是**——它的开销约等于

```
Σ_requests ( 该请求的新 token 数 × 该请求自己的 context 长度 )
```

同样 8192 个新 token，摊给 4 个各带 100K context 的请求，就是 **4 个独立的 score matrix**，indexer 的活是 1 个请求时的约 4 倍，而 GEMM 一动不动。

## 这正好是我们测量的一个缺口

SIKL 的 `prefill_conc()` **硬编码成每个 attention rank 一个请求**，它的注释也承认不建模 packing。而部署那边：

| | |
|---|---|
| `max_running_requests`（prefill leg） | **64** |
| AgentX CONC | 40，摊到 4 个 DP rank = **每 rank 10 个** |
| 每请求平均实算 | ~4,663 token |
| 每 rank chunk 预算 | 8,192 |

**4,663 × 2 ≈ 9,326 > 8,192。** 也就是说真实 scheduler 很可能在一次 forward 里 pack **约 2 个**长上下文请求——而我们测的是 1 个。

如果是这样，**我们报告里 `attn.indexer` 的 12.2% 是被低估的**，而 `mlp.experts`、`attn.o_proj` 那些行不受影响，所以整个排名会往 indexer 倾斜。

**我把这条标成假设，不是结论。** 要证实它需要两件事，都不难：

1. 从 packup 的 `server_metrics_export.json`（1.3 GB，还在 gitignore 的工作区里）确认 prefill batch 的实际 request 数分布
2. 用 `quick_test_prefill` 跑 `BATCH_SIZE` 扫描：固定总 token 数，把请求数从 1 变到 4，看 indexer 是不是线性涨而 GEMM 平

这就回答了你上一个问题——**batch size 不是 quick_test_prefill 的一个附带功能，它是 SIKL 结构上给不了、而我们恰好需要的那个维度。**

要我去查第 1 条吗？那份 metrics 应该能直接给出答案，不用花 GPU。

# AMD Spur Cluster Usage (crsuse2-m2m / amd-spur)

## Overview

This cluster does **not** run stock Slurm — it runs **Spur** (AMD's open-source, AI-native scheduler, `github.com/ROCm/spur`, Apache-2.0). Spur ships Slurm-compatible commands (`sbatch`, `srun`, `squeue`, `sinfo`, `sacct`, `scontrol`) plus a native `spur <subcommand>` CLI. Most Slurm muscle memory works, but a few flags differ — see Gotchas.

Verified on this cluster: `spur 0.9.1`, single partition `amd-spur`, ~256 nodes, **8× AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) per node**, 236 CPUs and ~2.8 TB RAM per node.

## Cluster Facts (quick reference)

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Scheduler | Spur 0.9.1 (Slurm-compatible) |
| Partition | `amd-spur` (only one; unlimited time) |
| GPU model | AMD Instinct MI355X, `gfx950`, 8 per node |
| Node specs | 236 CPU, ~2.8 TB RAM |
| Login GPU visibility | via `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (not `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`) |
| Binaries | `/usr/local/bin/{spur,sbatch,srun,squeue,sinfo,sacct,scontrol,scancel}` |

## Choosing your account (and the partition trap)

Jobs require `-A <account> -p amd-spur`. **The team names are _accounts_, not partitions.** There is exactly one partition, `amd-spur`; each team is an account listed under its `AllowAccounts`. Passing your team name as the partition fails:

```text
$ srun -A amd-primus -p amd-primus -t 1 hostname
Error: job submission failed
    message: "partition 'amd-primus' not found"
```

Rule of thumb: pick your team for `-A`, but **always** use `-p amd-spur`. Find which account(s) you belong to:

```bash
spur share | awk -v u="$USER" '/^[a-z]/{a=$1} $1==u{print a}'
```

Known team accounts (from cluster docs): `amd-general`, `amd-primus`, `amd-aifw-dev`, `amd-aifw-aim`, `amd-aifw-di`, `amd-silo-tiger`, `amd-aac`, `amd-frameworks-ci`. You can only submit under an account you're associated with — using someone else's is rejected (`user '<you>' is not associated with account '<x>'`).

## The rules that matter more than anything else

### 1. Do NOT request GPUs. `-N<n>` is the whole ask.

You get **all 8 GPUs of every node you're given**, for free, with no `-G` / `--gpus` /
`--gpus-per-node` / `--gres` flag at all. Adding a GPU flag only makes the request harder
to schedule — it does not get you more hardware.

```bash
sbatch -p amd-spur -q amd-primus-qos -N1 -t 04:00:00 job.sh    # ← correct: no GPU flag
```

Verified 2026-09-01 on job `94842` (submitted with `-N1` and nothing else): inside the
allocation `rocm-smi` lists **8 MI355X**, and `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is **empty** — empty
means *unrestricted*, not "no GPUs". Don't read an empty `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` as a
failure; run `rocm-smi` to see what you actually have.

### 2. `amd-burst-qos` is the LOWEST-priority QOS. Under contention it starves.

Its huge node cap (`node=182`) is bait: its **`Priority` is `100`, while every team QOS is
`10000`** — burst is preemptible surplus capacity, so the moment the cluster fills up, burst
jobs sort to the back of the queue and sit at `PENDING (Resources)` indefinitely.

```text
$ spur accounts show qos
Name                Priority  ...  GrpTRES
amd-burst-qos       100            node=182     ← big cap, bottom priority
amd-primus-qos      10000          node=16      ← your team: 100× the priority
amd-collectives-qos 10000          node=64
amd-general-qos     10000          node=8
```

**Default to your own team's QOS** (`spur share | awk -v u="$USER" '/^[a-z]/{a=$1} $1==u{print a}'`
→ append `-qos`). Reach for `amd-burst-qos` only when you need **more nodes than your team cap
allows** and can tolerate waiting/preemption.

Verified 2026-09-01, back to back on a full cluster (0 idle nodes, 157 `alloc`, 192 queued):
`-q amd-burst-qos -N2` sat `PENDING (Resources)` for minutes; two `-q amd-primus-qos -N1`
jobs both went `RUNNING` within 10 s. **Also prefer several 1-node jobs over one N-node job**
— single-node requests fit into gaps that a multi-node gang-schedule can't.

### 3. Want N *distinct* machines? Exclude the nodes you already got.

Nodes here are **shared**, so independently-submitted 1-node jobs happily land on the **same**
node — you end up with two job IDs and one machine. Submit them **serially**, excluding what
you already hold:

```bash
J1=$(sbatch --parsable -p amd-spur -q amd-primus-qos -N1 -t 08:00:00 hold.sh)
N1=$(squeue -j "$J1" -h -o "%N")                     # wait until non-empty
J2=$(sbatch --parsable -p amd-spur -q amd-primus-qos -N1 -t 08:00:00 -x "$N1" hold.sh)
squeue -u "$USER" -o "%i %j %T %N"                   # confirm two different nodes
```

Verified 2026-09-01: two jobs fired back-to-back both landed on `crsuse2-m2m-188`; resubmitting
the second with `-x crsuse2-m2m-188` got `crsuse2-m2m-115`. **Always check `%N` — don't assume
two job IDs mean two machines.**

### 4. A held node dies when its script exits — size `sleep` to the walltime.

For sleeper/hold jobs, the job ends when the **script** ends, regardless of remaining walltime.
`sleep 14400` under `-t 08:00:00` still releases the node at 4 h. Match them (`-t 08:00:00` +
`sleep 28800`).

You **can** extend the walltime of a running job (`scontrol` has no symlink here — go through
`spur`):

```bash
spur scontrol update jobid=<jobid> TimeLimit=08:00:00   # absolute, not a delta
squeue -j <jobid> -o "%i %l %M"                         # verify TIME_LIMIT actually changed
```

Verified 2026-09-01: this succeeded on a running job (`4:00:00` → `8:00:00`). **But it does not
extend the script** — a job still sleeping `14400` exits at 4 h anyway. To genuinely hold longer,
submit a replacement job (excluding your current node) before the old one expires.

## When jobs get stuck at `JobHoldMaxRequeue` — the two real causes

If a job flips to `PENDING Reason=JobHoldMaxRequeue` within seconds of submitting, it is **almost never** your account/GPU-count/walltime. Two things actually cause it, and both have concrete fixes:

**1. Bad compute nodes that `NODE_FAIL` every GPU launch (most common).** Some nodes accept placement but fail the job at launch on the node side; the job requeues and instantly hits the requeue cap → held. These nodes stay `idle` precisely *because* they bounce every job, and the scheduler keeps preferring them (they look free). Symptom: `spur diag` shows a large, climbing `NODE_FAIL` count; a job shows `Reason=None` on a node for ~1s then `JobHoldMaxRequeue`. **Fix: blacklist them.** Catch the node each held job landed on (`squeue -j <job> -h -o "%N"`), then resubmit with `--exclude=<node1,node2,...>`. A few rounds of excluding bad nodes lands you on a good one. Always verify you actually held it: `spur exec <job> true` must succeed (a job can show `RUNNING` for one poll then requeue — that's not a real hold).

**2. Your account's QOS is over its node budget** (`node=N` cap per QOS, `spur accounts show qos`). When your team QOS is saturated (or you're racing a job-flooding system like the `hyperloom`/`forge` auto-submitter), new jobs lose the launch race. Fix: ask for fewer nodes, or — if you truly need more nodes than the team cap — move to `amd-burst-qos`, accepting its bottom priority (see the QOS rule above). Note this is a *different* symptom from plain `PENDING (Resources)`: that one is priority/contention, not a hold.

**Don't pass `-A` unless you need to.** It defaults to your own account, and the verified-good invocation omits it entirely — just set the QOS:

```bash
sbatch -p amd-spur -q amd-primus-qos -N1 -t 08:00:00 job.sh
```

Verified good: this exact form (no `-A`, no GPU flag) schedules immediately even on a full cluster. Only add `-A <account>` if you belong to more than one and must pick a specific one. QOS is set with `-q/--qos` on **`sbatch`** (NOT `srun` — see Gotchas). Combine fixes when the cluster is busy: `-q <team>-qos --exclude=<bad nodes>`.

> Diagnosing which cause: `spur diag` for the `NODE_FAIL` trend; watch one job second-by-second (`scontrol show job <j> | grep -oE "JobState=[A-Z]+ +Reason=[A-Za-z]+"`) to see if it's bouncing off nodes vs. never placing at all. Bisect by fixing one variable at a time (GPU count, walltime, QOS, node) — don't assume.

## Submitting jobs

### Interactive one-off (srun) — the fast path for a quick job

**For a small/near-zero-resource job (a `helloworld`, a smoke test), just use `srun` — do NOT bother with `sbatch` + QOS.** `srun` runs under your **default** QOS, so you never have to think about QOS selection at all. Nodes here are **shared, not exclusive** — a `mix` node (there are usually dozens) has a running job on only a couple of its 8 GPUs / 236 CPUs, so a 1-GPU job drops straight into a free slot. **Verified good, dispatched and finished in seconds:**
```bash
# 1-GPU helloworld — the reliable quick smoke test (verified: schedules instantly)
srun -p amd-spur -N1 -G1 -t 00:01:00 \
  bash -c 'echo "helloworld from $(hostname), ROCR=$ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES"'
# → helloworld from crsuse2-m2m-047, ROCR=0

# check the GPU is really there
srun -p amd-spur -N1 -G1 -t 00:02:00 \
  bash -c 'echo ROCR=$ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES; rocm-smi --showproductname'
```
Notes:
- **`-G1` here is an `srun`-only exception.** For a fire-and-forget `srun` smoke test, asking for exactly 1 GPU packs into a busy `mix` node; a pure-CPU `srun` (no `-G`) can hang in `PENDING`. This does **not** apply to `sbatch` — there you pass no GPU flag at all (see the rule near the top).
- `srun` **rejects `--qos`/`--pty`** (see Gotchas) — that's fine here, default QOS is exactly what makes the quick path work.
- Don't pass `-A` — it defaults to your account (`amd-primus` for this user).
- Output streams straight back to your terminal; there's no `~/spur-<jobid>.out` file for `srun` (that's an `sbatch`-only thing).

### Batch (sbatch)
Don't hardcode `--account` (defaults to your own) and **don't request GPUs** — `--nodes` is the
whole ask, and you get all 8 GPUs per node. Set the QOS to your **team** QOS:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=myjob
#SBATCH --partition=amd-spur
#SBATCH --qos=amd-primus-qos
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --time=00:30:00

echo "Job $SLURM_JOB_ID on $(hostname)"
rocm-smi                      # ← 8 MI355X, even with no GPU flag requested
```
```bash
sbatch myjob.sh            # or: sbatch --parsable myjob.sh  → prints just the job ID
```
Need two machines? Submit **two 1-node jobs**, not one `-N2` job — they schedule far more
readily. If jobs get held at `JobHoldMaxRequeue`, see that section above (bad nodes → `--exclude`).

**Do NOT rely on `--output`/`--error`.** Spur's `sbatch` *silently ignores* them — set them and your logs vanish (job COMPLETEs, no file appears anywhere). Instead spur always writes a **combined** stdout+stderr file to `~/spur-<jobid>.out`. To capture logs where you want them, redirect inside the script (`exec > "$HOME/logs/$SLURM_JOB_ID.log" 2>&1`) or read `~/spur-<jobid>.out` afterward. (Verified: job with explicit `--output` produced zero files; job without it wrote `~/spur-<jobid>.out`.)

## Running Docker containers (the standard workflow here)

**This is how teams actually run workloads (vLLM, ROCm, etc.) on this cluster.** Do NOT use spur's native `--container-image` flag — it's broken here (see Gotchas). Instead, each compute node runs its own full Docker daemon (`dockerd` v29.6.x, root dir `/mnt/m2m_nobackup/docker`), and you drive it directly.

Why this works: a spur job's script (and any `srun` command) executes **on the host, as your own user**, not inside a wrapper container — so `docker` connects straight to the node's daemon. Verified: an sbatch script reported `whoami=yihou`, `pid1=bash`, and `docker version` showed `client=server=29.6.1`.

### Docker inside an sbatch script (recommended)
Put the `docker run` right in your job script. Spur gives you the node's GPUs without any GPU flag; you pass them into the container the ROCm way (`/dev/dri` + `/dev/kfd`, **not** `--gpus`).

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --partition=amd-spur
#SBATCH --qos=amd-primus-qos
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --time=04:00:00

docker run --rm \
  --device /dev/dri --device /dev/kfd --group-add video \
  --ipc=host --shm-size=16g \
  -v "$HOME:$HOME" -w "$HOME" \
  vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.24.0 \
  bash -c 'your_command_here'
```
```bash
sbatch myjob.sh          # logs land in ~/spur-<jobid>.out
```

### Docker interactively (grab a node, then poke at it)
```bash
# 1. hold a node (keep this in a real terminal / tmux — the alloc dies with it)
spur alloc -p amd-spur -q amd-primus-qos -N1 -t 04:00:00
# …or submit a sleeper job and note its <jobid>:
#   JOB=$(sbatch --parsable -p amd-spur -q amd-primus-qos -N1 -t 04:00:00 <(echo -e '#!/bin/bash\nsleep 14400'))

# 2. hop onto the node (needs a REAL terminal), then use docker normally
spur exec <jobid> bash
#   docker ps
#   docker run --rm -it --device /dev/dri --device /dev/kfd --group-add video \
#     vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.24.0 bash
```

Notes that will save you time:
- **`docker` images and containers are node-local** (`/mnt/m2m_nobackup/docker`), not on your NFS `$HOME`. A container you started on one node isn't visible from another. `docker ps` on a shared node shows *everyone's* containers — don't kill ones that aren't yours.
- **Mount your work in**: `-v "$HOME:$HOME"` (NFS home is mounted on every node), or bind a scratch path you need.
- **GPUs**: nothing to reserve (you get the node's 8); expose them with `--device /dev/dri --device /dev/kfd --group-add video`. Add `--ipc=host --shm-size=16g` for multi-GPU / large-tensor workloads (vLLM needs it).

## Monitoring & control

```bash
squeue                       # all jobs
squeue -j <jobid> -h -o "%T" # one job's state (PENDING/RUNNING/…)
sacct -j <jobid> --format=JobID,JobName,Account,State,Elapsed
scancel <jobid>              # cancel
spur exec <jobid> <cmd>      # run a command inside a running job's container (like docker exec)
spur attach --output-only <jobid>   # watch a running job's stdout/stderr
```

### Getting a shell on a running job
There is **no `srun --pty`** and **no `salloc`**. To get onto a running job's node, use `spur exec` with a **real terminal**:
```bash
spur exec <jobid> bash          # interactive shell — must run in a real TTY (piping/wrapping hangs it)
spur exec <jobid> rocm-smi      # one-off command
```
Two sharp corners: it runs **as root with `pwd=/`** inside the job's container (`cd` to your workdir first), and the interactive shell needs a genuine TTY — without one, `bash` just gets EOF and exits immediately instead of giving you a prompt (run it in a real terminal, not piped/wrapped).

> For multi-round work — iterating on a script, debugging a failing run, poking at a model/server — **prefer holding one node and `spur exec`-ing into it repeatedly** over re-submitting a job each round. See the **spur-interactive-debug** skill.

## Inspecting the cluster

```bash
sinfo                                    # partition/state summary
sinfo -h -o "%t %D" | awk '{a[$1]+=$2}END{for(s in a)print s,a[s]}'  # nodes per state
scontrol show node <nodename> | grep Gres   # GPU model/count on a node
# GPU model histogram across all nodes:
scontrol show nodes | grep -oP 'gpu:\K[a-z0-9]+' | sort | uniq -c
```
Node states: `idle` (free), `mix` (partly used, still schedulable), `alloc` (full), `resv` (reserved), `drain` (offline/maintenance).

## Gotchas

- **`srun` rejects `--qos` (and `--pty`).** Stock-Slurm docs here show `--qos=<account>-qos`, but `srun` errors with `unexpected argument '--qos'`. **`sbatch` _does_ accept `-q/--qos`** (verified) — use your **team** QOS there, not `amd-burst-qos` (see the QOS rule near the top). `srun` has no QOS flag, so for GPU work prefer `sbatch` + a held node + `spur exec`. Likewise `srun --pty` is rejected; there's no PTY on `srun` (use `spur exec` for a shell, above).
- **Don't pass `-G`/`--gpus*`/`--gres` on `sbatch`** — `-N<n>` already gets you all 8 GPUs per node; GPU flags only make scheduling harder. See the rule near the top.
- **An empty `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` means unrestricted, not "no GPUs."** Use `rocm-smi` to see what you actually have. (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is likewise usually empty here — ignore it.)
- **`sacctmgr`/`sshare`/`salloc` aren't standalone binaries** — use `spur accounts` / `spur share` / `spur alloc` (or the `spur <subcmd>` form). For an interactive allocation: `spur alloc -A <acct> -p amd-spur -t 12:00:00`.
- **`sbatch --output`/`--error` are silently ignored** — logs always go to `~/spur-<jobid>.out` (combined stdout+stderr). Setting an explicit output path makes logs vanish. See the sbatch section above.
- **`ssh <compute-node>` is blocked for normal users — and the error lies.** It returns `Permission denied (publickey)`, which looks like a key problem, but the real cause (per the node's own sshd log: `User <you> not allowed because not listed in AllowUsers`) is an `AllowUsers ubuntu root` whitelist in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-compute-node-access.conf` on each node. Your key is fine — sshd rejects you at preauth by username before ever checking it. This whitelist was **added 2026-07-22** (previously ssh-with-a-key worked, which is why older docs say to just add a key — that advice is now stale). Fixing it requires an admin to add you to `AllowUsers` on every node; you can't self-serve it. **Use `spur exec` instead** (it goes through spurd, bypassing sshd entirely). For multi-node torchrun/MPI that needs rank-to-rank SSH, ask an admin or use spur's native multi-node mechanism. (This is a live admin-controlled policy — re-check the sshd log if behavior changes.)
- **Jobs stuck at `JobHoldMaxRequeue`?** Usually **bad NODE_FAIL nodes** or a **saturated QOS**, not your flags — see that section above (fix: `--exclude` the bad nodes). Distinguish it from plain **`PENDING (Resources)`**, which is a priority/contention problem: drop `amd-burst-qos` for your team QOS, drop GPU flags, and split `-N2` into two `-N1` jobs.
- **Containers → use plain Docker, see "Running Docker containers" above.** Spur's _native_ container path (`spur image import` + `--container-image`/`--container-*` job flags) appears broken here — avoid it; run `docker` directly inside your allocation instead. (Note: a held job is far more likely the NODE_FAIL/QOS issue above than this.)
- Native extras beyond Slurm: `spur crontab` (recurring jobs), `spur health`, `spur net` (WireGuard mesh). (`spur image` exists but see the container note above.)

## Verify a working submission end-to-end

```bash
JOB=$(sbatch --parsable myjob.sh)
squeue -j "$JOB"                       # watch until it disappears (done)
cat ~/spur-$JOB.out                    # spur's combined stdout+stderr (NOT a --output path)
sacct -j "$JOB" --format=JobID,State,Elapsed
```

# SGLang internal decode bench & profiling

Benchmark and profile **decode** of a GLM-5.2-class model by calling SGLang's internals directly —
**no HTTP server, no Scheduler, no PD path**. The harness drives `TpModelWorker` + `EAGLEWorkerV2`
itself and spawns its own TP ranks, so a data point costs ~6 minutes instead of a full server bring-up.

This directory is the **single shared copy**. It used to be three divergent copies scattered across
per-experiment workspaces; those are now under `../temp_workspace/` and hold **no code**.

```
bench/      the engine — this is what actually runs
scripts/    runners and helpers (container, single point, sweep, profile, verify)
tests/      unit tests for the engine's pure logic
```

---

## What it does, and what it does not

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ real model weights, real MoE routing, real attention backends | |
| ✅ real EAGLE speculative decode (steps=5 / draft=6 / topk=1) | |
| ✅ CUDA-graph capture and replay, exactly as the server does | |
| ⚠️ **synthetic prefix** — KV is filled with physically valid random data, not a real prefill | |
| ⚠️ **simulated acceptance** — accept length is driven to a target, not sampled from the dr …[truncated]

---

## Profiling

`--profile` is **opt-in and off by default**; with it absent the harness is byte-compatible with the
published throughput results (the new flags are not even recorded in `config_yihou.json`).

Three mechanisms, so both CUDA-graph modes are covered:

| mechanism | graph ON | graph OFF | yields |
|---|---|---|---|
| `torch.profiler` over a window of iterations | ✅ | ✅ | per-kernel table + chrome trace |
| `DeviceTimer` (CUDA events, attached by the bench) | ✅ | ✅ | per-stage GPU seconds, whole run |
| `--enable-profile-cuda-graph` | ✅ | n/a | capture-time kernel **inventory** |

Outputs land in `<iteration>/profile/`: `*.trace.json.gz` (per emitting rank),
`top_ops_rank_N_yihou.{json,txt}`, `device_timer_rank_N_yihou.json`, `profile_meta_yihou.json`.

### Five rules that will otherwise give you wrong numbers

1. **Use `top_by_self_device_time_device_kernels_only`.** The sibling `top_by_self_device_time`
   includes `record_function` spans, which torch reports as `DeviceType.CUDA` rows that **overlap
   the kernels beneath them**. Sort naively and `step[TARGET_VERIFY bs=32]` ranks first at 838 ms
   while containing most of the list.
2. **A profiled run is not a performance measurement** (`is_performance_measurement: false`). Quote
   TPOT only from a non-profiled run.
3. **Attribute in the same graph mode as the configuration you care about.** Graph-ON gives the
   kernel layer but no CPU-operator layer and no `grid`/`block` args; graph-OFF gives both. Differ …[truncated]
```

README.md:43:Prefill has no concurrency or chunk-size flag, because neither is a free choice there. The chunk is `--chunked-prefill-size` read back *after* sglang resolves it — from HBM when unset (16384 on MI355X), then divided by `dp_size` since each DP rank schedules for itself, so `65536` under DP 8 gives every rank 8192 exactly as the server would. And a request longer than that budget ends the batch by itself, which leaves one request per attention rank. Shorter requests would be packed alongside others, which this bench does not model; the report's chunk timeline states the shape it measured so the assumption stays checkable.
README.md:62:The external check is `bench_serving`'s median ITL at the same shape — mean ITL and TPOT both fold in interleaved prefill chunks. At TP8 + DP8, `fp8_e4m3` KV, CONC 16:
README.md:92:| layers | 78: dense 0–2, MoE 3–77; layer 78 is the MTP draft (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLMNextN`) |
README.md:127:**Record, then replay.** Operator inputs are not built by hand: a `register_forward_pre_hook` records every module's real arguments during one real forward, along with what it reads off the forward state, and the module is then called on its own with that input. Re-deriving each operator's shape, dtype and `ForwardBatch` field by hand would not raise when wrong — it would just skew the number. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Create the owned container for the TP8/EP8/DPA decode point on this bare-metal host.
# Adapted from packups/glm52_tp4_noep_dpa_sweep_yihou.packup_20260911-1100/scripts/create_container_yihou.sh:
# the slurm/spur allocation guards and the crsuse2-m2m node guards are removed (this host is ours and
# has no scheduler); everything that affects the measurement is kept identical.
set -euo pipefail

TOOL_ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$TOOL_ROOT/.." && pwd)   # bind-mounted into the container

CONTAINER=${CONTAINER:-yihou-glm52-tp8ep8-0914}
[[ "$CONTAINER" =~ ^yihou-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ]] || { printf 'Container name must start with yihou-: %s\n' "$CONTAINER" >&2; exit 2; }

"""ROCm opt-out for SGLang's CUDA-only DSA ``topk_v2`` JIT kernel.

The supported SGLang releases default ``SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2`` ON, but that kernel's
header includes ``<cooperative_groups.h>`` (CUDA-only; ROCm ships only
``hip/hip_cooperative_groups.h``), so hipcc fails at JIT time and the engine
dies in decode CUDA-graph capture. Upstream turns the flag off on HIP only in
the ``DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`` branch of ``server_args.py``, yet the kernel is
shared by every DSA arch — GLM-5.x, DeepseekV32, LongcatFlash, MistralLarge3 —
which therefore still hit it. Default it OFF on ROCm instead; the backend then
takes the legacy ROCm transform path.

Set-if-unset, so it self-retires: once upstream guards the kernel, its own value
(or an explicit ``SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=1``) wins and this becomes a no-op.

Verified 2026-07-30, MI355X/gfx950, GLM-5.1-FP8 tp4:
capture dies at 0/4 without it, completes 4/4 with it.

import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_ROCM_DSA_DEFAULTS: dict[str, str] = {
    "SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2": "0",  # sglang reads this as EnvBool (default True)
}

):

        batch.global_num_tokens = [mlp_sync_info.num_tokens]

def prepare_dp_metadata(batch, topology, *, is_extend, disable_cuda_graph):
    # ScheduleBatch counts are BASE requests. The pinned ForwardBatch scales them

- 部署：decode 节点 TP4 / attn-DP4 / EP1，EAGLE 5/6/1（模拟接受长度 3.61），fp8 KV，page 64，DSA 用 triton，`--disable-custom-all-reduce`。

## assistant · 2026-10-09T03:13:00.718Z

Batch size 是按请求数算的。主测点和变体如下：

| 测点 | 除 DP 前（全局，`--batch-size`） | 除 DP 后（每个 attn-DP rank） | 每 rank 的 verify / draft-extend token 数 | 每 rank 的 MoE 输入 token 数（汇总 4 个 DP rank 后） |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 主测点 P1/P2/P3/P5 及 graph-ON 排名 | **16** | **4** | 24（每请求 6 个 token） | 96 |
| 变体 P4 | **24** | **6** | 36 | 144 |

**依据**
- 选值来自线上 decode 日志的 `#running-req`，取 profiling 窗口内 7,356 行。日志每行带 `DP3 TP3` 这样的 rank 前缀，所以这个数本身就是除 DP 后的每 rank 值。分布是：众数 3，p50 4，p90 6，最大 15。我取 p50=4 作为主测点，p90=6 作为变体，再乘 4 个 DP rank 得到全局的 16 和 24。
- 除 DP 后确实是 4：工具里 `local_batch_size = batch_size // dp_size = 16 // 4 = 4`。shape 抓取的记录也对得上，TARGET_VERIFY 是 batch 4、24 个 token，CUDA graph 也是按 bs=[4] 捕获的。

**和线上的差别**
- 工具里 4 个 DP rank 都是同样的 4 个请求。线上各 rank 的请求数并不相等，所以 MoE 汇总后的 token 数是各 rank 之和，不一定是 4×24。
- 每个请求的上下文统一设成 110K。线上 decode 时每个请求的上下文 p50 约 237K，更长一些；我只用 P2（240K）验证过，上下文变化只影响 indexer 相关的 shape。

# Repository conventions

## DCO sign-off is required on every commit

This repository enforces the [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org/).
CI blocks any PR containing a commit without a `Signed-off-by:` trailer, so an
unsigned commit is a broken PR, not a style nit.

Commit with `-s`, always:

```bash
git commit -s -m "..."
git commit -s -F -   # when writing a longer message from a heredoc
```

That appends a trailer built from **your own** `user.name` / `user.email`:

```
Signed-off-by: Your Name <you@example.com>
```

**Sign off as yourself.** The DCO is an assertion that *you* have the right to
submit this code, so the trailer must name the person making the commit. Never
copy a colleague's line from an existing commit, and never use a bot or assistant
identity — contributors here sign off under several different addresses, and the
trailer has to match the commit's actual author.

Check what `-s` will produce before your first commit in a fresh clone or
container, where git may have inherited a default from the environment:

```bash
git config user.name && git config user.email
```

If those are empty or wrong, set them (add `--global` outside a container):

```bash
git config user.name "Your Name"
git config user.email "you@example.com"
```

### Fixing commits that are already missing it

Sign off a range without disturbing commits that already carry the trailer —
rebasing from a point that includes signed commits appends duplicates:

```bash
git rebase --signoff <last-already-signed-commit>
git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>
```

Pick `<last-already-signed-commit>` as the newest commit that already has the
trailer. Check what you are about to touch first:

```bash
git log --format='%h %s | %(trailers:key=Signed-off-by,valueonly)' origin/main..HEAD
```

Cherry-picks do **not** inherit the trailer — `git cherry-pick -s`, or sign off
afterwards. This is the easiest way to reintroduce the problem on a second branch
after fixing it on the first.

## Related trailers

`Signed-off-by` is the DCO assertion and is mandatory. `Co-Authored-By` is
separate, is not a substitute, and some upstreams reject assistant co-author
trailers outright — when contributing to a third-party repository (e.g. ROCm/aiter),
do not add them.

20	**How.** Success = **the output artifact exists AND the log contains no
21	`Traceback`**. `rm -f` the `--out` path first so a stale artifact cannot read as
22	a pass. In the checker use `|| true` plus an empty-check, never `|| echo 0`.
23	
24	**Context.** The false green is the dangerous one — it would have carried an
25	empty report forward. It was caught by a monitoring teammate within minutes, not
26	by the exit code. **Read the artifact, never the status.**
27	
28	---
29	
30	## 2. `--chunked-prefill-size` must be 8192 here, and the reason is not obvious
31	
32	**What.** This parameter was set wrong, then corrected wrong, then corrected
33	again. Final answer: **pass 8192**, even though the deployment's CLI passed
34	32768.
35	
36	**Why.** Two separate facts collide. (a) Under DP attention sglang divides the
37	flag by `dp_size` — so `server-info.json`'s `8192` is the **post-division**
38	value, not the flag. (b) But in this sglang the division lands only in the
39	**published bag**; `parallel_hook.py` calls `declare_resolution(...)`, which does
40	**not** mutate the `ServerArgs` dataclass — and SIKL's `chunk_tokens()` reads the
41	raw dataclass attribute. SIKL's docstring claims the older mutate-in-place
42	behaviour and is **stale**.
43	
44	**How.** Verify rather than reason — the three-line probe in `REPRODUCE.md` §4
45	prints `RAW 32768 BAG 8192`.
46	
47	**Context.** The cost of getting it wrong is invisible: at 32768 point B would
48	have run **4 chunks instead of 13**, producing a plausible-looking wrong-shape
49	result, and the per-chunk growth table — the whole finding — would have been
50	built on it. The smoke could not have caught it: at ISL 8192 the chunk is
51	`min(budget, ISL)` either way.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 3. Dropping the argument would have been worse than the crash
56	
57	**What.** Upstream SIKL calls `initialize_moe_config(server_args)`; this sglang's
58	takes **no** argument, so it raises `TypeError` and the run dies in `setup()`.
59	
60	**Why.** sglang moved runtime configuration behind a **published context**. The
61	initialisers now read `get_exec()/get_spec()/get_flags()` and must be called
62	**after** `publish(server_args, role=...)`.
63	
64	**How.** Mirror the image's own `sglang/benchmark/one_batch.py::latency_test`
65	(lines 903-909): `publish(...)` first, then the three no-arg initialisers.
66	
67	**Context.** This is the trap worth internalising. The obvious fix — delete the
68	argument — makes the crash go away and the run **succeed while silently wrong**:
69	a spawned TP child arrives with nothing published, so the MoE and quant flags
70	resolve from **defaults** rather than from our server args, skewing exactly the
71	`mlp.experts` row the bench exists to measure. `latency_test` even carries the
72	comment "a spawned child arrives with nothing published." **A crash you can see
73	is safer than a default you cannot.**
74	
75	---
76	
77	## 4. SIKL vendors its own `aiter`, and it is not the one you want
78	
79	**What.** Putting `/workspace/SIKL` on `PYTHONPATH` — the documented usage —
80	makes `import aiter` resolve to **SIKL's vendored copy**, which differs from the
81	image's in **205 paths including `fused_moe.py`** and six tuned-GEMM CSVs.
82	
83	**Why.** `fused_moe.py` is the kernel behind `mlp.experts`, ~19 % of TTFT. You
84	would be measuring SIKL's MoE kernel instead of the one the deployment runs.
85	
86	**How.** `PYTHONPATH=$FORK:/sgl-workspace/aiter:/sgl-workspace/sglang/python` —
87	no `/workspace/SIKL`. Confirm via the report's Versions table:
88	`aiter 4ad998328+dirty` is the image's.
89	
90	**Context.** The only cost is that the `sikl` package becomes unimportable, so
91	SIKL schema dumps are unavailable. Nothing here needed them.
92	
93	---
94	
95	## 5. `kill -9` on the parent orphans four ranks that `pkill` cannot find
96	
97	**What.** After `kill -9`, four rank children survived on **44 % VRAM across all
98	four GPUs** at ~130 % CPU each.
99	
100	**Why.** They are bare `multiprocessing.spawn` processes — **their argv contains
101	no `profile_prefill.py`**, so the obvious `pkill -f profile_prefill.py` misses
102	every one. What normally reaps them is `common.run()`'s
103	`finally: kill_process_tree(os.getpid(), include_parent=False)`, and `-9` skips
104	the `finally`.
105	
106	**How.** Stop runs with the **default signal**. If you must clean up, match
107	`multiprocessing.spawn`. Verify GPUs are back to 0 % before relaunching.
108	
109	**Context.** The failure mode is not "a stuck process" — it is that the *next*
110	run either OOMs or, worse, contends and produces slow-but-plausible numbers.
111	Every exit also logs `destroy_process_group() was not called`, so there are two
112	independent reasons never to assume a clean release between runs.
113	
114	---
115	
116	## 6. Log lines that look alarming and are not
117	
118	| line | verdict |
119	|---|---|
120	| `[AR] All-reduce call path: NCCL (custom AR disabled)` | **benign** — this is the **world** group, which hardcodes `use_custom_allreduce=False`. The TP group logs `[AR] Using AiterCustomAllreduce (AMD default)` alongside it. Both appear 4x per run. Confirmed by direct read: `tp_group.ca_comm is not None = True`. |
121	| `Using FP8 KV cache but no scaling factors provided` | expected for `fp8_e4m3` without calibration; the deployment's prefill leg takes the same path |
122	| `destroy_process_group() was not called` | cosmetic at exit — but see trap 5 |
123	| `Ignore import error when loading sglang.srt.models.mamba` | sglang logs it as ignorable |
124	| `Disable prefill CUDA graph` | **required** — SIKL forces `--disable-cuda-graph` so its pre-hooks fire; graph replay runs no Python |
125	| `chunked prefill size is adjusted from 8192 to 2048` | sglang dividing into its published bag, which SIKL never reads — see trap 2 |
126	
127	---
128	
129	## 7. `patch -p0` does not apply these diffs
130	
131	**What.** `REPRODUCE.md` originally said `patch -p0 < ...`. It applies nothing
132	and exits 1.
133	
134	**Why.** Both diffs were generated with `diff -u <abs> <abs>`, so they carry
135	**absolute paths** on both sides; `-p0` strips nothing and GNU patch refuses the
136	absolute path outright (`Ignoring potentially dangerous file name`). `cwd` is
137	irrelevant, so the `cd` in the instructions bought nothing.
138	
139	**How.** Name the target: `patch common.py < <diff>`. Verified to rebuild the
140	fork **md5-identically** from stock SIKL `82dd439d`.
141	
142	**Context.** The failure is at least **safe** — patch refuses rather than
143	silently re-patching. Also note `cp -r SRC DST` nests the copy as `DST/glm52`
144	when `DST` exists; use `cp -r SRC/. DST/`.
145	
146	---
147	
148	## 8. Two wrong turns worth recording, because both were mine
149	
150	**The structural argument I invented.** I argued that `mlp.<rest>` sat outside
151	the residual coupling that made `attn.<rest>` and `layer.<rest>` swing against
152	each other. `common.py:948` says otherwise:
153	`RESIDUALS["layer"] = ["input_layernorm", "attn", "post_attention_layernorm", "mlp"]`
154	— `layer.<rest>` subtracts the `mlp` parent exactly as it subtracts `attn`.
155	**Identical coupling; `mlp.<rest>` simply did not move that time.** The
156	conclusion survived, the justification did not. Caught by a reviewer who went and
157	read the code instead of accepting the argument.
158	
159	**A claim of conformance that the data contradicted.** I wrote that the
160	directly-measured rows reproduced "inside SIKL's claimed band" of 0.2-0.5 % —
161	while my own table two lines below showed `attn.fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` at
162	**-1.60 %**, and `attn.o_proj` and `attn.q_b_proj` already past 0.5 %. We do not
163	meet that band and the analysis now says so.
164	
165	**The pattern in both:** reasoning from a remembered claim instead of the
166	artifact in front of me. The same pattern produced two misreadings from the
167	monitoring side — grepping one string and generalising from it. Everything that
168	went wrong today was caught by going back to the **primary source**: the image's
169	own `one_batch.py`, `parallel_hook.py`, `common.py`, or the raw log of the run
170	actually being claimed about.
171	
172	---
173	
174	## 9. Timing and resource expectations
175	
176	- Weight load stragglers **2.5x across ranks in the same run**: TP1 186 s,
177	  TP2 189 s, **TP0 460 s**, all landing at 119.24 GB `quant=quark`. Budget by
178	  the worst rank. Possibly related to deviation 6 (affinity never set) and to
179	  GPUs 4-7 being on NUMA 1 — **plausible, unverified.**
180	- First bring-up pays a **cold aiter JIT compile** that looks like a hang. The
181	  cache reached 218 MB and was reused thereafter — paid once.
182	- Point A / A2 ≈ 13 min each; point B ≈ 28 min.
183	- **Never pipe these logs through `tail`** — they carry multi-megabyte
184	  single-line tqdm bars. Use `wc -l` then `sed -n 'N,Mp' | cut -c1-200`.
185
